articles.title: Tamil Nadu: Vijay govt disbands DMK-formed Centre-State panel, shifts mandate to Law Commission
articles.description: The C Joseph Vijay-led TVK government has disbanded the High-Level Committee on Centre-State Relations, headed by retired Justice Kurian Joseph, triggering criticism from several political parties and public voices. The move is yet another instance of the government’s knee-jerk decision-making, with announcements often made in the morning only to be withdrawn or reversed by evening, night or the following day, reflecting its failure to study decisions in depth before announcing them. One netizen pointed out: “The reasoning in this order is that this is not a statutory body. But the fact is that neither the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission nor the Law Commission of India are statutory bodies; both are constituted by executive orders.” Breaking: @TVKVijayHQ government winds up the High Level Committee on Centre – State relations! After dithering for six months, @CMOTamilnadu via the Public Department, winds up the Commission ! Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay proves, yet again, by his actions that he is scared… pic.twitter.com/hCxOgGZ8eM — RadhakrishnanRK, PhD. (@RKRadhakrishn) November 7, 2026 Following the disbanding of the Kurian Joseph-led committee, the Vijay government constituted a new Law Commission on August 7, 2026, under Government Order No. 202, Law (LC) Department, with the stated objective of making work relating to Union-State relations more effective. The decision followed consultations with experts. The new commission is headed by former Manipur High Court Chief Justice T. Krishnakumar, with former Madras High Court judge Justice Deeka Raman, former Additional Chief Secretary T.K. Ramachandran, IAS, and former Law Department Secretary A. Arunagiri as full-time members. Former District Judges P. Mohandas and R. Govindarajan have been appointed as part-time members. Also Read: Diwali is not ‘Eid of Happiness’: Know the cultural identity behind festival of lights DMK attacks TVK government; BJP welcomes decision Several political parties, including the DMK, CPI and Dravidar Kazhagam, criticised the TVK-led government for disbanding the High-Level Committee headed by retired Justice Kurian Joseph on Central -State Relations. DMK president MK Stalin said: “The TVK government says yes to ‘theatre rights’, while saying no to ‘state rights’ by disbanding the committee,” referring to the government’s decision to increase film screenings. However, Tamil Nadu BJP chief spokesperson Narayanan Thirupathi welcomed the decision. He said: “The decision of the Tamil Nadu government under Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to disband the High-Level Committee on Union–State Relations is a welcome and practical step. The committee, constituted by the previous DMK regime, was unnecessary.” The decision of the Tamil Nadu @TVKPartyHQ government under Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay @CMOTamilnadu @TVKVijayHQ to disband the High-Level Committee on Union–State Relations is a welcome and practical step. The committee, constituted by the previous @arivalayam regime,… — Narayanan Thirupathy (@narayanantbjp) November 7, 2026 The panel members were reportedly each being paid a salary of Rs 5 lakh per month, apart from other perks. The committee had 3 members. Kurien Joseph ( who is a good man ) , Ashok Vardhan Shetty ( dmk mouth piece ) , M . Naganathan ( Stalin family sidekick ). Each were being paid salary of 5 lakhs per month apart from other perks. For what joy , I don’t understand. Tamil Nadu state highways dept cancels two of its first-of-its-kind tenders to allow private maintenance of highways for a short term contract of six months. Reason cited: No response from L1 bidder. In both tenders, four contractors participated and one contractor emerged as… pic.twitter.com/PIAS65UFPL — Omjasvin M D (@omjasvinMD) November 8, 2026 Temple mobile phone restrictions eased after opposition Following strong opposition, the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) Department of the TVK government eased the restrictions on carrying mobile phones inside temples. On October 14, the TVK government announced a relaxation of the restrictions on carrying mobile phones inside 52 temples across Tamil Nadu, allowing devotees to take their phones inside, provided they are switched off. However, photography, videography and selfies remain prohibited. The restrictions had come into effect on September 1. TN govt exempts public (law and order) dept from RTI act. Cites that it is an intelligence and security organisation. pic.twitter.com/SwyGSenAIW — Omjasvin M D (@omjasvinMD) September 27, 2026 The controversial GO would have blocked access to records relating to custodial deaths, communal clashes and security-related detentions. It specified the Public (Law and Order) Department as an intelligence and security organisation established by the State government, to which the RTI Act would not apply under Section 24 of the Act. The department deals with communal clashes, agitations involving political parties, students and agricultural labourers, and requests for the withdrawal of cases registered on political grounds. articles.title: Odisha strengthens Water Security, Irrigation and Energy Infrastructure: Cabinet Approves Projects Worth Over ₹5,098 cr
articles.description: Bhubaneswar: In a major push towards strengthening water security, agricultural productivity and energy infrastructure, the Odisha Cabinet has approved three significant projects covering Balangir, Nuapada and Kalahandi districts. The initiatives, involving an overall investment of over ₹5,098 crore, aim to ensure sustainable water availability, expand irrigation potential and enhance the state's renewable energy storage capacity. In-stream Storage Structure on Indra/Sundar River in Balangir The Cabinet has approved the tender for construction of an in-stream storage structure across the Indra/Sundar River, a tributary of the Tel River, near village Patharla in Titilagarh block of Balangir district, at an execution cost of ₹99.99 crore (excluding GST). The project is targeted for completion within 30 calendar months. The project aims to conserve monsoon runoff by creating in-stream water storage, making the stored water available during lean seasons. It will provide assured and sustainable domestic water supply to around 12 villages across Titilagarh and Bangomunda blocks. In addition, it will support animal husbandry, fisheries and other water-dependent livelihood activities, while contributing to ecological balance and groundwater recharge. Seven Mega Lift Irrigation Schemes in Nuapada In another significant decision, the Cabinet has approved the tender for seven Mega Lift Irrigation Schemes under Cluster XXVIII of the Parbati Giri Mega Lift Irrigation Project in Nuapada district, with a total financial outlay of ₹289.68 crore. This includes ₹268.22 crore towards execution and ₹21.46 crore for 15 years of operation and maintenance. The seven schemes—Boden, Borigaon, Khairmal, Lasunpali, Gandabahali, Chaura and Konabira—will create an additional planned irrigation potential of 8,800 hectares across 59 villages in Boden, Sinapali and Komna blocks. Drawing water from Udanti River and Lower Indra reservoir, the schemes will extend irrigation facilities to upland agricultural areas that are difficult to serve through conventional gravity-based systems. The schemes will provide pressurised irrigation through underground pipelines up to the one-hectare chak level, reducing water losses, promoting micro-irrigation, improving productivity and encouraging crop diversification. Fully state-funded, they will be implemented over 36 months with 15 years of operation and maintenance. 600 MW Upper Indravati Pumped Storage Project in Kalahandi The Cabinet has approved the project cost, EPC contractor and financial framework for the 600 MW Upper Indravati Pumped Storage Project at Ranibahal, Kalahandi, to be implemented through Odisha Hydro Power Corporation Limited (OHPC). M/s Megha Engineering & Infrastructures Ltd. (MEIL) has been selected as the EPC contractor at ₹3,372.88 crore (excluding GST). The total project cost is ₹4,708.64 crore, covering consultancy, land acquisition, forest clearances and interest during construction (IDC). The project will follow an 80:20 debt-equity ratio, with OHPC contributing 20% equity from its internal reserves and the State Government providing the remaining 80% as a phased soft loan at an interest rate at par with the RBI repo rate. The 600 MW facility will generate 1,040 MU of annual peak energy using 1,283 MU of off-peak pumping energy. It will store surplus power and supply it during peak demand, while enhancing grid stability through frequency response, spinning reserves, load management and black-start capabilities. The project is scheduled for commissioning by FY 2030-31.

articles.title: Bright Outdoor Media lists on BSE, NSE main boards after SME stint
articles.description: New Delhi: Bright Outdoor Media has been listed on the main boards of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE). The company announced the move in a regulatory filing on November 6. The Mumbai-based out-of-home (OOH) advertising company was earlier listed on the BSE SME platform. It debuted there on March 24, 2023. The company says it was the first outdoor media firm to list on an Indian stock exchange. Bright Outdoor Media runs more than 1,350 hoardings. It also owns over 50 large-format digital LED billboards in Mumbai. The company has secured the advertising tender for the Navi Mumbai Metro Line. It also operates advertising inventory under an Indian Railways tender for the Vile Parle to Kandivali road overbridge. Its Bright 360 initiative offers integrated branding and advertising services. The company plans to grow this business further. Its other priorities include adding hoardings and digital displays. It also plans to target government, railway and transit projects. It will explore new geographies and solar-powered advertising infrastructure. Dr Yogesh Lakhani, CMD, Bright Outdoor Media, said the main board listing was a significant moment for the company. He said the company aims to build a larger outdoor advertising business. Its focus will be on digital innovation and infrastructure-led projects. For FY26, the company reported total revenue of Rs 155.43 crore. EBITDA stood at Rs 35.23 crore. Net profit was Rs 24.05 crore. In H2 FY26, total revenue was Rs 92.12 crore. Net profit for the period was Rs 13.97 crore. Founded in 1980, the company is headquartered in Andheri, Mumbai.

articles.title: MSME Ministry reviews CPSE procurement from SC/ST enterprises to meet mandated target
articles.description: Central Public Sector Enterprises gathered in the national capital to assess and accelerate their procurement compliance under the mandated four per cent target reserved for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Micro and Small Enterprises, according to the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME).
